_comment: The local gate's backend on its node (the Pro). Copy to ~/.config/cortados/local-backend.json ON THE PRO (or point CORTADOS_LOCAL_BACKEND_CONFIG / the gate's --backend-config at it). No file = Ollama, no governor (the gate as before). backend: "ollama" | "vllm-mlx"; switching is this one value plus a gate restart (docs/LOCAL-RESOURCES.md, MLX backend: switch and rollback). The model path is config: a 6-bit copy is another vllm_mlx.models entry and vllm_mlx.model names the one served. Read by cortados_router/local_backend.py; scripts/install_mlx_backend.sh builds the vllm-mlx LaunchAgent from it.
_read_timeout_s: The gate's wait for each upstream read (default 300 s). A non-streaming vllm-mlx answer sends nothing until it is whole; at 8 at once a long one takes minutes. 900 matches vllm_mlx.serve.timeout_s. Set the Pro block's read_timeout_s on the provider host to the same.

vllm_mlx._comment: venv: the Python venv holding vllm-mlx (0.6.0 measured). served_model_name must be the id the provider's config gives this model on the Air (tables/resources.json, the Pro block's models[].id), so nothing changes there but max_inflight; name and name:latest are the same model. idle_cap, weights_bytes, kv_bytes_per_token, per_seq_state_bytes, prefill_margin_bytes and context_tokens size the governor per model (governor._reasons has each one's reason). serve: vllm-mlx flags (local_backend.SERVE_DEFAULTS has each one's reason); host must be loopback. extra_args: only the flags in local_backend.EXTRA_ARGS_ALLOWED (sampling defaults, --stream-interval, --chunked-prefill-tokens, --disable-prefix-cache); anything the generator sets (host, port, max-num-seqs, max-tokens, ...) or any other flag is refused.

qwen-27b-4bit._comment: Measured 2026-11-14 on the Pro: peak aggregate 87.9 tok/s at 8, 31 GB peak footprint (~8.5k-token prompts). weights_bytes 15 GiB. KV: 16 full-attention layers x K/V x 4 KV heads x head_dim 256 x fp16 = 65,536 bytes/token (a 128k context holds 8 GiB), plus ~0.15 GiB recurrent state per sequence; vllm-mlx keeps the KV cache unquantized.

_reasons.max_images: Owner decision 2026-11-15/16: up to 5 still images per request.
_reasons.image_tokens_max: Each image at most 1,024 language-model tokens (~1 MP after the processor's resize: 16-pixel patches merged 2x2 are 1,024 pixels per token). The guard sets the processor's max_pixels to 1,048,576; upstream's 16.7 MP would be 16,384 tokens and 1 GiB of KV cache per image. 64 MiB of KV per image at 65,536 B/token.
_reasons.image_context_tokens: Image-bearing requests capped at 64k combined context (input + max_tokens) until measured; the guard refuses a longer one exactly after counting its image tokens.
_reasons.image_concurrency: One image-bearing request at a time until measured (vision encoding is the unmeasured peak); text turns still run beside it under the owner's count.
_reasons.max_image_bytes: 5 MiB decoded per image: the Anthropic API's own per-image limit, so a turn the cloud takes fits here too.
_reasons.max_image_pixels: 32 Mi decoded pixels per image from the file header, before anything is decoded (an 8K screenshot fits); PIL's bomb limit is set to the same.
_reasons.prefill_chunk_tokens: The guard prefills an image-bearing prompt in chunks of this many tokens, projecting only the last position to the vocabulary (upstream: one atomic forward projecting every position, 27.8 GiB of logits at 60k tokens). head_dim 256 is outside MLX's fused attention kernel, so a chunk holds heads x chunk x context scores: 256 keeps them at 3 GiB at the 64k image context.
_reasons.score_buffers: Score-sized buffers per chunk: q.k^T, the masked copy, the softmax output, and one the allocator holds from the previous layer.
_reasons.act_bytes: bfloat16 activations; the guard refuses a model whose config.json names a wider dtype.
_reasons._encoder: vision_num_heads, vision_depth: the vision tower's heads and blocks (vision_config num_heads, depth). 1,152 / 16 = head_dim 72, inside MLX's fused attention (64/80/128), so the encoder holds no heads x N x N scores; the guard refuses a model whose head_dim is over 128, and the gate counts those scores (encoder_scores) whenever fusion is not provable.
_reasons._dims: hidden_size .. vision_depth: the model's config.json text_config and vision_config widths the reservation is computed from (local_governor.image_prefill_bytes). The guard is passed them (--image-dims) and stops vision mode unless config.json has exactly these: a different model needs the reservation recomputed. Values are the public Qwen3.5-27B layout; the Pro's own config.json is checked at startup.
_reasons._acceptance: The image reservation is a computed upper bound (docs/LOCAL-RESOURCES.md "Vision"). The real-model peak measured in the hardware test window (64k image context, 5 images; and the reviewer's ~60k tokens + one small image) is the acceptance gate for these numbers.

qwen-27b-4bit-vision._comment: PROVISIONAL until measured on the Pro (the production switch needs the owner's approval after measurements): the 4-bit language weights plus the BF16 vision tower (qwen3_5, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration). weights_bytes = the 4-bit entry's 15 GiB + ~1.5 GiB assumed for the tower: replace with the measured resident size. The guard runs in vision mode for this entry (local_backend.vision_argv).

qwen-27b-6bit._comment: Memory measured on the Pro: 22.4 GB idle (weights_bytes), peaks 24.7 / 25.9 / 27.9 / 31.5 GB at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 requests of ~8.5k tokens. Same architecture as the 4-bit, so the same KV and state sizes; 17.6 GiB beside the weights holds one 128k-token request (9.65 GiB reserved), not two. Throughput not benched: idle_cap stays 6 until it is. Set path to the copy's directory.

governor._comment: Activity governor (cortados_router/local_governor.py, owner-approved policy; docs/LOCAL-RESOURCES.md "MLX backend"). Enforced in the local gate on POST /v1/messages by two bounds: a COUNT from the owner's activity and memory pressure, and a BYTE budget: each request reserves (input tokens + max_tokens, capped at context_tokens; input tokens bounded from above by the request body's bytes as received plus a chat-template allowance and what vllm-mlx re-serializes wider, never an estimate) x kv_bytes_per_token + per_seq_state_bytes + prefill_margin_bytes, and is admitted only while the reservations in flight fit in memory_budget_bytes - weights_bytes. A request over either bound now gets a retryable 529 with Retry-After; one that could not fit even alone gets a non-retryable 413 (the provider routes it elsewhere). Nothing is queued at the gate, running requests are never stopped. Remove the section to run without a governor (unlimited, as with Ollama).

_reasons.active_idle_s: 10 minutes without keyboard or mouse: the owner has stepped away (a pause to read or think is shorter); below it the owner is active and the laptop must stay responsive.
_reasons.active_cap: Owner active: measured on the Pro (4-bit, ~8.5k-token prompts) 2 requests give 47.8 tok/s aggregate at 23.9 tok/s each, near single-request speed; 4 already drops each to 18.7 tok/s and TTFT to 43 s.
_reasons.idle_cap: Owner idle and pressure normal: the per-model cap (each vllm_mlx.models entry sets its own). Default 8, the measured aggregate peak for the 4-bit model (87.9 tok/s at a 31 GB peak, no swap growth; 16 fell to 64.8).
_reasons.warn_cap: Memory pressure warn: macOS is compressing and close to swapping; hold at 1 running so the node drains instead of adding KV cache.
_reasons.critical_cap: Memory pressure critical: admit nothing new; running requests finish (stopping them would waste their work and free memory no sooner).
_reasons.sample_s: Signals are re-read at most every 5 s: idle changes on a scale of minutes, pressure of seconds; never one subprocess per request.
_reasons.retry_after_s: Retry-After on an over-limit 529: the next sample is at most sample_s away and a slot frees when a request ends; 5 s lets a client retry soon without hammering the gate.
_reasons.unknown_pressure: An unreadable pressure level counts as warn: keep serving one at a time rather than stopping (critical) or trusting an unknown memory state (normal).
_reasons.memory_budget_bytes: 40 GiB (42949672960) of the Pro's 48 GB unified memory for the backend, leaving ~8 GB for macOS and the owner's apps. Requests are admitted only while the bytes they reserve, in flight together, fit in memory_budget_bytes - weights_bytes.
_reasons.weights_bytes: Default resident weights when a model entry names none: the 4-bit 27B is 15 GiB (16106127360); the 6-bit entry sets its measured 22.4 GB.
_reasons.kv_bytes_per_token: KV cache per token of context, unquantized fp16 in vllm-mlx: Qwen3.8 27B keeps KV only in its 16 full-attention layers: 16 x 2 (K, V) x 4 KV heads x head_dim 256 x 2 bytes = 65,536, so a 128k-token request holds 8 GiB.
_reasons.per_seq_state_bytes: Per running request whatever its length: the hybrid model's recurrent-layer state, about 0.15 GiB (161061273) per sequence.
_reasons.prefill_margin_bytes: Per running request: prefill activations and allocator slack beyond KV and state. The 6-bit copy used 2.3 GB over idle for one ~9k-token request, of which KV + state explain ~0.7 GiB; 1.5 GiB (1610612736) covers the rest. A 128k request then reserves 9.65 GiB: two fit in 25 GiB, a third does not; eight ~9k-token requests (2.2 GiB each) do.
_reasons.context_tokens: The longest context the model is served with, the Pro block's context_length on the provider host (131072). A request's tokens (input + max_tokens) are capped here.
_reasons.default_max_tokens: max_tokens reserved for a request that names none: vllm-mlx's own default (vllm_mlx.serve.max_tokens, 32768; the gate takes the serve value when this key is absent).
